notes: Full ready->working->waiting->working->ready arc for a GENUINELY human-decided permission gate (--approval-judge off; see metadata.json caveats — this is a load-bearing recipe precondition, not the default profile). Single-birth session model (muse's session id = directory basename, fixed at session start), so session_birth anchors to "start" unpinned; every later phase is pinned same_session_as:session_birth because muse spawns companion child sessions freely during any turn (2-2 and 2-17 both hit a vacuous pass from an unpinned phase silently matching a subagent's own arc instead of the primary session's). No cost is ever persisted for muse-spark-1.3-contributor (no pricing/alias entry), so cost_nonzero is false; tokens are used every model call, so tokens_nonzero is true.

text: Session appears in ready shortly after the muse TUI finishes launching (--trust-workspace skips the first-run trust dialog)
muse-bin PID bound to the real session via its .session.lock held flock fd
User prompt drives ready -> working (run.started -> EventType=user_message) on the same session that was born ready

The bash tool call (touch/rm -rf/echo) needs approval under --approval-judge off; kind:"approval" "requested" opens with presentation_phase:human_pending, TranscriptPermissionPending -> waiting via state_classifier.go's transcript_permission_prompt rule. Live probe on this machine took ~20-25s of model thinking/tool-call setup before the approval modal actually opened, hence the generous window.

The driver's raw keypress ("1" = Allow this stage once, no trailing Enter) answers the prompt; kind:"approval" "decision_applied" (decision_source.kind expected human_approval) closes it and the session returns to working while the approved command actually runs and the agent continues toward its final reply

invariants: no state_transition to waiting after this phase
text: Turn completes back to ready on the same session once the final reply (PERMISSION_GATE_OK) lands; state must not bounce back to waiting afterward (the muse analog of the claudecode scenario's 'late hook does not reopen waiting' criterion — muse has no hook channel, so this instead asserts the transcript-driven pairing is idempotent and terminal)
